pairs.subject: dependency-declaration
pairs.evidence: src/features/vault/sub_dependencies/credentialGraph.ts:373 This context gets the credential-to-persona edges as a ready-made input (computed by the backend command credential_dependents_all from tool_connector bindings and audit-log rows in src-tauri/db/src/repos/resources/audit_log.rs) and only lays them out, analyses blast radius and simulates revocation. It neither designs nor runs a way for units to declare or resolve their own dependencies. A case-insensitive search of the context directory for manifest, lockfile, vendor, peerDependenc, importmap, package.json and resolver found nothing.

techniques.evidence: src/features/vault/sub_dependencies/CredentialRelationshipGraph.tsx:44 The whole edge set is fetched up front for display. It is a runtime view snapshot, not a stored or committed closure standing in for anyone's declarations, so the enumerate-or-traverse choice and the reaper/currency check it calls for have nothing to apply to here.

src/features/vault/sub_dependencies/credentialGraph.ts:384 The only name lookup in the context picks a connector's display colour, with a fallback colour if none is found. It is not a reference-resolution layer that decides which artifact a dependency points to.

src/features/vault/sub_dependencies/credentialGraph.ts:440 Link types (tool_connector/event_trigger/audit_log) arrive already attached to each edge from the backend. Where the declaration lives, and who writes it, is decided in the persona config and db repo, not here.

pairs.registryProposal: The context matcher seems to have paired this subject with the context because of the word 'dependencies' in its name (sub_dependencies, a credential relationship graph). That is a domain meaning of dependency (which agent uses which credential), not the software meaning (how a unit declares its requirements). Weighting the subject's own vocabulary (manifest, resolver, declaration, import) above the bare token 'dependency' would avoid this false match.
